newsitem.title: USA: Judge rules for Penthouse in military case.
newsitem.headline: Judge rules for Penthouse in military case.

text.p: A federal judge ruled on Wednesday that a new law banning the sale of sexually explicit material at government-operated military stores violates the First Amendment.

In a victory for Penthouse magazine that challenged the law, U.S. District Judge Shira Scheindlin ordered that the Department of Defense be permanently restrained from changing the military's existing stock or selling policies.

General Media Communications Inc., which publishes Penthouse, and a group of trade associations sued the Department of Defense in October to block enforcement of the Military Honor and Decency Act that restricts the dissemination of "sexually explicit material" within the U.S. military.

The law was enacted on Sept. 23, 1996, when it was signed by President Bill Clinton. It had been scheduled to take effect on Dec. 22, but Scheindlin issued a restraining order on Dec. 20 temporarily blocking the Defense Department from enforcing the provisions.
The act's provisions prohibit the sale or rental of such material on property controlled by the Defense Department including commissaries and ship stores.
It also bans the sale or rental of such material by a member of the Armed Forces or a civilian officer or employee acting in an official capacity.
